description: A team is using a phased rollout and needs to decide what signals over the next few days should trigger pause, continue, rollback, or intensified monitoring instead of treating launch as a one-time event.

user_profile.context: The code is already live for part of the user base, so the key challenge is interpreting rollout signals well
user_profile.communication_style: Observational and threshold-based, prefers operational criteria over intuition

fact_sheet.fact: The software release is NexusDB version v4.7.1, which introduces the 'Real-time Query Cache' (RQC) feature.
The lead product engineer for the v4.7.1 RQC rollout is Alex Chen.
The main tracking ticket for this release is in Jira under the ID NEX-1138.
The Git commit hash for the v4.7.1 release build is `a1b2c3d4e5f67890a1b2c3d4e5f67890a1b2c3d4`.
The phased rollout began on October 26, 2023, at 10:00 UTC.
The RQC feature is currently enabled for 10% of users in the `us-east-1` region.
The next planned stage is to increase the rollout to 25% of `us-east-1` users on October 28, 2023, at 14:00 UTC.
The feature is controlled by a feature flag named `enable-realtime-query-cache` in the 'LaunchDarkly' platform.
The initial rollout cohort is limited to users on the 'Free-Tier' subscription plan.
The primary monitoring dashboard for the rollout is Grafana Dashboard ID `nexus-rqc-rollout`, accessible at `https://grafana.quantumleap.tech/d/nexus-rqc-rollout`.
The key success metric is 'Cache Hit Rate', with a target of over 85%.
All critical alerts related to the rollout are routed to the Slack channel `#nexus-alerts`.
A key stability metric being monitored is the P99 query latency for reads.
The Splunk query to search for new fatal errors is `index=nexusdb level=FATAL error_code=CacheConsistencyViolation`.
A full rollback is automatically triggered if the P99 query latency exceeds 500ms for 5 consecutive minutes.
The rollout will be paused if the API 5xx error rate increases by more than 20% over the baseline for a 10-minute window.
The rollout is considered safe to continue to the next phase if all key metrics remain within +/- 5% of their baseline for 4 continuous hours.
Intensified monitoring is initiated if the cache hit rate drops below 90% but remains above the rollback threshold of 80%.
The discovery of any new `CacheConsistencyViolation` error type in the logs requires an immediate manual rollback.
The current on-call engineer for the Core Platform Team is Priya Sharma, contactable on Slack at `@priya.sharma`.
The on-call engineer has full authority to initiate a rollback without requiring management approval.
A daily rollout status meeting occurs at 09:00 PST via the Google Meet link `meet.google.com/xyz-abc-def`.
All decisions to pause, continue, or rollback are documented in the Confluence 'RQC Rollout Log' page, ID `7891234`.
The command-line tool for managing the deployment is named `deployment-cli`.
The specific command to execute a rollback is `./deployment-cli rollback --service nexusdb --version 4.7.0 --feature-flag enable-realtime-query-cache=false`.

The daily rollout status meeting at 09:00 PST is used to review the current rollout percentage and cohort, check key signals such as cache hit rate, P99 query latency, API 5xx error rate, and any new `CacheConsistencyViolation` events, and decide whether to continue, pause, rollback, or move to intensified monitoring for the next phase.

user_needs.description: What is the current rollout status for the NexusDB v4.7.1 release, including start time, current percentage, and region?
Which specific user cohort is part of the initial rollout?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After understanding the general rollout status, the user would want to know the specific audience affected.

user_needs.description: Where can I find the primary monitoring dashboard for this rollout?
What is the key success metric and its target value?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: Once the user accesses the dashboard, their immediate next step is to understand what 'good' looks like.

user_needs.description: What is the automatic rollback condition related to P99 query latency?
What is the condition for pausing the rollout based on the API 5xx error rate?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After understanding one critical failure condition (latency), the user will want to know about other key failure conditions like error rates.

user_needs.description: What is the Splunk query for the specific error type that requires an immediate manual rollback?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: Following questions about threshold-based alerts, the user would want to know how to find specific, non-threshold-based critical errors.

user_needs.description: Under what conditions is the rollout considered safe to continue to the next phase?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After learning the success metric (what is good), the user will naturally want to know the criteria for proceeding (how good is good enough).

user_needs.description: When is the next rollout stage planned and what is the target percentage?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After learning the criteria for continuing, the user will want to know the schedule for the next step.

user_needs.description: What is the threshold for initiating intensified monitoring?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After asking about the primary success metric, it is helpful to proactively provide information on the 'warning' threshold that isn't a failure but requires closer attention.

user_needs.description: What is the specific command-line instruction to execute a rollback?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After learning about a condition that requires a manual rollback, the user might need the exact command to perform that action.

user_needs.description: Who is the current on-call engineer and what is their authority regarding rollbacks?
Where are all rollout decisions documented?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After identifying the person responsible for making decisions, the user will likely want to know where those decisions are logged for audit purposes.

user_needs.description: Which Slack channel receives critical alerts for this rollout?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After learning how to query for fatal errors, a natural follow-up is to ask where automated alerts for such issues are sent.

user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After establishing which Slack channel receives critical rollout alerts, a natural next communication question is the schedule and working agenda of the daily rollout status meeting where those signals are reviewed.
